newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada maintains gold policy despite no new sales.
newsitem.headline: Canada maintains gold policy despite no new sales.

text.p: The government of Canada has stopped selling off its gold reserves for the past three months, but officials said on Wednesday that there has been no change in policy.
"The policy is to sell the gold," an official at the Department of Finance said in an interview.
"The pace depends on market developments," the official explained. "The decision to sell gold is really based on the return to holding gold versus the return to selling gold."
As of February 28, the government's gold holdings stood at 3.1 million ounces, the department said in a statement.

The government has a longstanding policy of gradually selling off its gold reserves and replacing them with interest-bearing assets. Gold reserves have dwindled from about 22 million ounces in 1979, the official said.
He would not say how low the government would allow reserves to fall.
"We do have a target, but that's not a number that we can discuss."
The Bank of Canada sells the gold on behalf of the government, and it weights market conditions to decide when more should be sold, he said.

The price of gold bullion has been low since the beginning of 1997. Gold was trading at about US$353.50 an ounce in New York on Wednesday. The price sank as low as US$339.60 on Feb 11, falling from US$367.80 on December 31.
